clue.text: Writers making cuts

definitions.meaning: journalists, especially jobbing ones churning out copy
chopping roughly, as with an axe

explanation.definitionFit: Hack is slang for a run-of-the-mill journalist, and to hack is to chop at something, so the plural noun and the verb share one spelling.

clue.text: American breakfast pot with toast on Sunday

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called hash
to toast bread is to brown it

explanation.surface: Someone in the US has a breakfast pot with toast on a Sunday morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like a cooking vessel but is the drug, and 'toast' is a verb here, not the bread itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Fried grated potato patties are a staple of the diner breakfast in the United States.

clue.text: It is often thrown after the match

definitions.text: It is often thrown after the match

parts.words: It is often thrown after the match
parts.note: the match is not a sporting fixture but a marriage, and guests shower the couple with paper pieces after the ceremony

explanation.definitionFit: Small scraps of coloured paper are tossed over newlyweds as they leave the wedding.

clue.text: A set hour for changing the division of spoils

indicators.note: changing tells us the letters of the phrase 'A set hour' are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a time at which the loot will be split up among the gang.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'changing' rearranges ASETHOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A share-out is the distribution of gains or booty among those entitled to a portion.

clue.text: View certain to be heard from the front

indicators.note: to be heard says the phrase for view-certain is spoken, giving a coastal word

parts.note: to view is to see, and certain means sure, giving see-sure

explanation.surface: A view that you are certain of, overheard from the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' is a link word; 'the front' is the seafront of a British resort, the promenade along the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: At a seaside town the front is the coastal strip where land meets the water.

clue.text: Fat little girl with tiny top

parts.note: Sue is a short girl's name, a diminutive of Susan

indicators.note: top of a word in a down clue is its first letter, here of tiny

explanation.surface: An unkind remark about a plump little girl wearing a very small top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like an adjective about the girl, but it is a noun: the hard animal fat used in puddings and pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Suet is the hard fat around beef and mutton kidneys, used in British cooking.

clue.text: Dish is served up outside tents

indicators.note: outside means the turned word wraps around the word for tents
in a down clue, served up means the word is is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a camp is a group of tents

explanation.surface: A meal is brought to diners sitting outside their tents at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' turns IS into SI, which goes outside CAMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaded langoustine tails are a familiar pub meal in Britain.

clue.text: Go faster under anaesthetic and manage

parts.note: someone under anaesthetic is unconscious, or out
to manage a business is to run it

explanation.surface: A patient told to speed up while still sedated and somehow cope.
explanation.definitionFit: To outrun someone is to exceed their speed and leave them behind.

clue.text: Set off across a point

indicators.note: across means the shuffled letters stretch over and round the letter a
off suggests the letters of Set are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets off across a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET to EST, which goes 'across' A to give E-A-ST.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the four cardinal compass bearings, the direction of sunrise.

clue.text: Star cricketer, he might do this on the beach

definitions.text: Star cricketer, he might do this on the beach

parts.note: the Sun is our nearest star
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A celebrated cricketer relaxing on the sand during a day off.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines while its first three words build the answer: a star cricketer lying on the sand would do exactly this.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in sunshine to tan is what a holidaymaker does on the sand.

clue.text: Private room on terrace initially? Rubbish

parts.note: Tommy is the traditional nickname for a British private soldier

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letters of room, on and terrace

explanation.surface: A soldier asks if there is a room on the terrace, and is told it is nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective about the room, but it is the soldier: TOMMY (from Tommy Atkins) is the British army private.
explanation.definitionFit: Tommyrot is an old British word for nonsense or foolish talk.

clue.text: Away leg not visible to audience

parts.note: away means off, as in gone
a leg of a journey is a stage

explanation.surface: Football-style talk of an away leg that viewers cannot see.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Away leg' suggests a cup tie played at the other team's ground, but the two words are split.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors in the wings are out of sight of the theatre's spectators.

clue.text: Plant involved in mash production?

parts.note: plant here is a factory, not a vegetable for mashing; mash is the grain and hot water steeped to make beer

explanation.definitionFit: A beer factory steeps malted grain in hot water to make mash before fermenting.

clue.text: You will shortly be heard — bound to be heard at Christmas

indicators.note: be heard tells us the contraction for you will is spoken, giving an old festive word

parts.note: you will shortened is you'll

indicators.note: to be heard says the word for bound is spoken, giving the word for a season

parts.note: bound means tied up

explanation.surface: A promise that you will soon be heard, certain to be heard over the festive period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word; 'bound' looks like 'certain to' but is TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is an old name for the festive season around 25 December.

clue.text: Genuine fungi need to be cooked

indicators.note: to be cooked tells us the letters of fungi need are mixed up like ingredients

explanation.surface: Real mushrooms have to be cooked before eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfeigned means not pretended, sincere.

clue.text: Courses need instructions

definitions.meaning: guidance on how to do or reach something

explanation.definitionFit: Directions can be the routes something takes or orders telling someone how to proceed.

clue.text: Whilst upset, root around for a quick itinerary

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of whilst upset root are spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: While annoyed, someone roots around for a short travel plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'around' rearranges WHILSTUPSETROOT, and 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief tour stopping only briefly at many places, as on a political campaign.

clue.text: Run into drunk, with a lot of points

indicators.note: into means the letter for run is put inside the word for drunk

parts.note: pickled is slang for drunk
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a drunk who has a lot of points to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a lot of points' means spiky, like a hedgehog.
explanation.definitionFit: Covered in thorns or spines, as a cactus or hedgehog is.

clue.text: Do veal, or otherwise it could be the last straw

definitions.text: it could be the last straw

indicators.note: otherwise tells us the letters of do veal or are arranged in a different way

explanation.surface: A cook is told to prepare the veal, or face the final provocation.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the burden that is finally too much, an excess beyond capacity.

clue.text: Studying the odds first, and expanding…

indicators.note: first means the odds abbreviation comes before the word for studying

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds in horse racing
studying means reading, as at university

explanation.surface: A punter studies the odds first, and widens bets.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the British betting term for the odds when a race begins. The ellipsis links to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Spreading out means extending over a wider area.

clue.text: No time to bother with foreign currency

indicators.note: No means the letter for time is removed from the word

parts.note: bother means trouble

explanation.surface: A traveller with no time to bother with exchanging money abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is the monetary unit of Russia.

clue.text: Some Mexicans like detectives to be noisy

indicators.note: to be noisy tells us as-tecs is spoken aloud to give a people's name

parts.note: like means as, and tecs is short for detectives

explanation.surface: Some Mexican people enjoy loud detectives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like' looks like a verb (enjoy) but is AS; TECS is old slang for detectives.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aztecs were a Nahuatl-speaking people of central Mexico before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: …but retaining right to extract

indicators.note: retaining means holding the letter for right inside

parts.note: but means except, as in all but one

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: yet keeping the right to extract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract' looks like a verb but is a noun, a passage taken from a longer text; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A short passage taken from a book, film or piece of music.

clue.text: Glove puppet finally — at last — let a gun go off

indicators.note: at last says that letter goes at the very end
go off tells us the letters of let a gun are scattered, like a gun firing
finally picks the last letter of puppet

explanation.surface: A glove puppet is finally allowed to fire a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glove puppet' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Glove' alone; 'at last' says the final letter of 'puppet' goes after the rearranged 'let a gun'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauntlet is a strong glove with a long cuff.

clue.text: First class touring car outside, but walk

indicators.note: outside means the touring car letters surround the first-class letters

parts.note: GT stands for gran turismo, a touring car
A1 means first class, written with I for the one

explanation.surface: A first-class driver tours in a car outside, but still walks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First class' is A1, with the figure 1 standing for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A gait is a manner of walking.

clue.text: Dainty material from Scotland — almost

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is cut off the word

parts.note: tweed is a rough woollen cloth from the Scottish Borders

explanation.surface: A delicate fabric, almost from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: TWEED takes its name from the River Tweed on the Scottish border.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively quaint or sweetly pretty.

clue.text: Rich source and a bit of bother

parts.note: a well is a source of water or oil
a to-do is a fuss or bit of bother

explanation.surface: A wealthy source of income causes some trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do describes people who are prosperous and comfortably off.

clue.text: Reuters? A puzzle and a thing to value

indicators.note: puzzle tells us the letters of Reuters and a are jumbled

explanation.surface: A news agency sets a puzzle, and something worth prizing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reuters' is the news agency, here only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is anything precious, a prized possession.

clue.text: Some old birds in a couple of parties begin to swoon

indicators.note: a couple of means the word for party is taken twice

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: begin to picks the first letter of swoon

explanation.surface: Some elderly ladies at a couple of parties start to faint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old birds' suggests elderly women, but the birds are extinct ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The flightless bird of Mauritius was hunted to extinction in the 17th century.
